thread.title: Is The Apple iPhone Lineup About To Get More Colorful?

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Is The Apple iPhone Lineup About To Get More Colorful?
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) could be looking to give sales of its midrange iPhone 8 a boost by adding a range of colors to its next-generation version this fall, an analyst said Monday.
X Details about the upcoming Apple iPhone lineup, due for release in September, are starting to leak out. Rosenblatt Securities analyst Jun Zhang said Apple could use colors to differentiate its 12th-generation smartphone lineup. One of those handsets could be an upgraded version of the current iPhone 8 called the iPhone 8S, he said.
"To target the younger consumer market, we believe that Apple could launch multiple colors for the iPhone 8S, including blue, yellow and pink, during the second half of this year," Zhang said in a note to clients.
Bright Colors The last time Apple tried the colored iPhone strategy was in 2013 with the iPhone 5C. That handset came in five bright colors: blue, green, pink, yellow and white. Since then, Apple has stuck with metallic-tone casings.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Apple is likely to use candy colors with its new LCD-screen smartphone to differentiate it from two high-end OLED-screen models coming out at the same time, he said.
"Given the success of the 5C, we believe this strategy could drive incremental demand for the LCD model," Zhang said. He estimates that the new LCD iPhones could account for half the new iPhones sold in the second half of the year.
3D Sensor On Back Of iPhone Apple also is likely to advance its push into augmented reality by adding 3D sensing cameras to the back of its new iPhones. Today only the high-end iPhone X has a 3D sensor and it's on the front of the device, with applications limited to facial identification.
Zhang reiterated his buy rating on Apple stock with a price target of 180.
Apple shares dipped slightly to close at 188.15 on the stock market today . On Thursday, the stock hit a record high of 190.37, after rising for nine consecutive trading days .
